text:
Alex Chen: Quick share — ran a controlled compare between two model variants with the replay harness + synthetic tail sampling. Short summary: baseline (v1) vs quantized (v1-q4f16) under identical prompts/decoding params. Seeing 12-18% median latency win for q4 but occasional 2-3% tail regressions when KV reuse hits a particular pattern.
Maria Gomez: nice. can you paste the harness config you used? especially batching and cache TTLs. :eyes:
Alex Chen: sure — config snippet below:
```
--mode=replay 
--batcher=continuous 
--max-batch-ms=8 
--kv-cache-ttl=60000 
--tokenizer=hf-bpe-v3 
--decode=topk=50,temp=0.7,stop=["\n","\n\n"]
```
Jin Park: that TTL is fine. the tail regressions smell like kernel selection thrash — when sequence lengths spike the runtime flips kernels and we lose warmup for fused attention. I instrumented a run with per-kernel time breakdown: fused-attn falls back to generic when seq>1024 for that model arch. sending snippet.
perf-bot: run 2219812345-1 completed (replay-bench). avg latency: v1=134ms, v1-q4=118ms, p50/p95/p99 reported. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/runs/2219812345-1
Samir Patel: @Maria is this an apples-to-apples decode? stop sequences aligned? tokenizer mapping same? small tokenization diffs can move alignment and impact KV reuse patterns.
Maria Gomez: good call. Alex, did you force the same tokenizer vocabulary and tokenization seed? if not, we should rerun with explicit tokenizer mapping.
Alex Chen: I explicitly used hf-bpe-v3 for both but didn't run a token-by-token alignment check. I did set identical decoding params (topk/temp/stop) and pinned random seeds for sampling. I'll generate a tokenization diff report.
Jin Park: also check that the replay harness isn't re-chunking inputs differently for quantized variant due to different eager-flush thresholds. We had a bug where small micro-batches were emitted earlier on q4 path.
Alex Chen: noted. I'll force batch flush consistency with `--enforce-batch-boundary` and re-run.
Maria Gomez: for methodology notes: please include (1) exact prompt corpus (sha256), (2) tokenizer version + sha, (3) decode params, (4) harness commit hash, (5) kernel-selection log snippet, (6) per-request KV hit/miss counts. We'll need that for any perf regression ticket.
Samir Patel: if you can, also capture per-request tokenization offsets so we can check stop-sequence placement. small off-by-one tokenization shifts explain some headroom differences.
Alex Chen: will do. quick Q: where should I upload the tokenization diff artifact? same s3 run dir?
perf-bot: artifact upload endpoint: s3://redwood-perf/runs/2219812345-1/artifacts/ (use folder token-diffs/)
Alex Chen: uploaded token-diff CSV and kernel logs to that path. re-run scheduled with enforced batch boundary now. ETA ~10m. :thumbsup:
replay-bot: scheduled replay job 2219812345-2 (enforce-batch-boundary=true) — status: queued.
Maria Gomez: great. once we have the second run, let's pull p95 breakdown by seq-len bucket (<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024) and compare kernel choices. if kernel flip correlates with tail spikes we should consider a warmup sticky policy for fused kernels.
Jin Park: yep — sticky policy or a tiny warmup micro-batch to prime kernels. also worth trying `--prefer-kernel=fused-attn` flag for an experiment.
Samir Patel: and keep the tokenizer alignment report in the ticket. if it's clean and we still see regressions, we can open an eng-runtime perf regression with kernel logs.
Alex Chen: thanks all — I'll post the results here when the queued run finishes. (reaction: :rocket:).
